answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to earn stake-backed reputation over time instead of spawning free identities at will. Like a trellis that only supports vines that actually grow along it, the network lets agents climb by completing verifiable work, while a short horizon of trust is extended only after repeated honest service. Newcomers start on a shared terrace with capped rewards, so creating many fake identities costs more than it earns and honest agents keep the upside.
